prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1284; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver of the rear-vehicle in a two-vehicle rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured reports slowing for traffic when struck from behind. No police report filed at scene; exchange of information completed. Assigned to me for handling.

Entry 2: Contacted the claimant, the driver of the front vehicle. Claimant reports pain and swelling in the right knee after impact, did not go to the scene hospital, and has since seen a primary care provider. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and says they are handling the claim personally. Explained the claims process and requested medical records and bills.

Entry 3: Reviewed photos submitted by both drivers. Rear bumper damage to the claimant's vehicle is consistent with a moderate-speed impact. Insured's front bumper shows minor scuffing. Estimate requested from the body shop for the claimant's vehicle. Liability appears clear on the insured's side based on the statements and damage pattern, pending final review.

Entry 4: Received the claimant's medical records from the primary care provider. Diagnosis noted as a right knee sprain with soft tissue involvement. Physical therapy was recommended, and an orthopedic follow-up is scheduled. Requested the itemized billing and a copy of the treatment plan. Will set a reserve for bodily injury pending the treatment outcome.

Entry 5: Spoke again with the claimant, who reports ongoing knee discomfort and is attending physical therapy about twice a week. Claimant asked about the timeline for settlement and was told that I cannot finalize an injury evaluation until treatment is complete. Advised the claimant of their right to review any settlement offer before signing. Diary set to follow up after the orthopedic visit.
